_doc: Findings a human has accepted for this release, each naming its card.
The smoke report is EVIDENCE and is never edited to make a gate pass. This
file is the separate, reviewable record of which findings were triaged and
consciously shipped with - so the acceptance is auditable, attributable and
sits next to the evidence rather than inside it.
The release skill's own rule: a pre-existing finding 'does not block - it
gets a card and a line in the audit file, so the delta stays honest'.
Rules the gate enforces, so this cannot become a dumping ground:
- every entry names a real card id and a reason;
- every entry names the version it is accepted FOR, and is ignored for any
other version, so an acceptance cannot silently carry forward;
- a finding in the report that is NOT listed here still blocks.
Accepting a finding is a decision someone made. Removing an entry is how you
`resolved` is NOT `accepted`. An accepted finding ships as-is. A resolved one
was FIXED after the walk recorded it, so the report is simply stale for that
entry - and the honest answer to a stale report is a re-walk. Where a re-walk
was not run, the entry must say exactly how the fix was verified instead, so a
reader can weigh that evidence rather than assume a walk covered it.

resolved.verified_by: Browser, Local site at Pro ff4c840: Sell Services > Settings loads with zero JS errors; #wpss-save-plan, #wpss-save-subscription-settings, #wpss-save-rule and #wpss-wl-save each have a click handler; clicking White Label Save sent wpss_pro_save_white_label and returned success 'Settings saved.'. tests/test-js-namespace-calls-defined.php fails on the old admin.js (WPSSPro.initStorageSettings() undefined) and passes on the fix.

The tip modal Cancel now carries wpss-btn--secondary like every other modal Cancel. tests/test-design-token-integrity.php section 8 (every .wpss-btn carries a variant) fails on the old template naming this button and passes on the fix.

A real inconsistency, not intended: the service card hid New for a complete profile while the vendor directory and profile always showed it, each with its own markup. All three now render templates/partials/vendor-level-badge.php and every level shows everywhere (journey 22 updated to say so). Verified on Docker at 1280 and 390, Pro on and off (surface vendor-badge); tests/test-vendor-level-badge-one-renderer.php fails on the old card.

The teaser text read --wpss-wp-admin-* tokens that do not flip in dark mode. Now design-system greys: measured 9.86:1 light and 12.71:1 dark on /dashboard/create/ on Docker at 1280 and 390 (surface dashboard-sections). Token test section 9 fails on the old pro-teaser.css and unified-dashboard.css.
